name: The Recon Maze
lesson: Spotting discovery: bursts of built-in admin commands from the wrong host or account, and internal sweeps for reachable systems.
pivot_tip: Pivot on host and user together. 'net group' from IT-ADM-03 is a Tuesday. From a finance desk as an IT admin, it's a hunt.
reaction: The sweep stopped and restarted from a different source port pattern. VELVET LOCUST is slowing down to blend in.

e501.title: UEBA: t.brooks on an unusual host
lines: ANOMALY  : Privileged account active on never-before-seen host   Risk: 92/100
Account  : HALCYON\t.brooks (IT-Admins, Server Operators, Backup Operators)
Host     : WS-FIN-0142 (finance)     Usual hosts: IT-ADM-03, JUMP-02
Activity : 6 discovery commands in 4 minutes (baseline: 0 on this host)
Note     : Logon type 9 (NewCredentials) from updchk.exe context
e501.tip: Logon type 9 means someone ran a program with alternate credentials. The stolen t.brooks password is being used.

e502.title: DC LDAP query log
lines: Expensive/inefficient LDAP queries (Event 1644) from 10.20.4.142 as t.brooks:
09:53:12  (&(objectCategory=group)(cn=Domain Admins))        attrs: member
09:53:18  (&(objectCategory=group)(cn=Backup Operators))     attrs: member
09:53:31  (objectCategory=computer)                          returned 412 entries
09:53:40  (&(objectCategory=user)(adminCount=1))             returned 9 entries
Baseline for 10.20.4.142: 0 such queries in 90 days
e502.tip: Enumerating admin groups and every computer is how an adversary draws their map. You can hunt for the mapping itself.

e503.title: Flow summary: 10.20.4.142 fan-out
lines: Source 10.20.4.142  09:56:02-09:56:40  distinct destinations: 8  ports: 445
Workstations normally talk to 2-3 internal servers. This one probed 8 hosts in 38 s.
Responsive servers: DC-01, FS-CORE-01, BACKUP-01, JUMP-02, VAULT-DB-01
e503.tip: Fan-out (one source to many destinations on the same port in seconds) is the fingerprint of a sweep.

e504.title: IT change calendar (Nov 17)
lines: 08:45  t.brooks  Password reset for j.reyes (ticket #48201)  - uses 'net user /domain'
10:00  t.brooks  Patch audit (Get-PatchStatus.ps1) on IT-ADM-03
No scheduled work on any WS-FIN-* host today.
Tom Brooks status: in the 09:30-11:00 budget meeting (calendar), laptop closed.
e504.tip: Legitimate admin activity has context: a ticket, a source host, a time. Tom was in a meeting during the discovery burst.

objectives.title: Read the behavior alert
hints: The Behavior Analytics node.
Press E at UEBA-01.
Open 'UEBA: t.brooks on an unusual host'.

objectives.title: What did 't.brooks' run on the finance desk?
objectives.desc: Hunt proc for everything the t.brooks account ran on WS-FIN-0142.
objectives.solution: search proc where host="WS-FIN-0142" and user="t.brooks"
objectives.success: whoami, net group, nltest, net view, a port sweep. Textbook discovery.
hints: Combine the host and the user.
host="WS-FIN-0142" and user="t.brooks".
search proc where host="WS-FIN-0142" and user="t.brooks"

objectives.title: Is this normal anywhere?
objectives.desc: Find every net.exe and nltest.exe run in the zone, so you can compare hosts. Try '| count by host'.
objectives.solution: search proc where name in ("net.exe", "nltest.exe") | count by host
objectives.success: IT-ADM-03 ran one, with a ticket. WS-FIN-0142 ran four in three minutes. Context is everything.
hints: The 'in' operator matches any value in a list.
Add '| count by host' to compare sources.
search proc where name in ("net.exe", "nltest.exe") | count by host

objectives.title: Map the sweep
objectives.desc: Find the connections from 10.20.4.142 to port 445.
objectives.solution: search net where src="10.20.4.142" and dport=445
objectives.success: Eight targets in 38 seconds. Five servers answered. Those are where they'll go next.
hints: SMB uses port 445.
Filter on the source IP and the destination port.
search net where src="10.20.4.142" and dport=445

objectives.title: Corroborate
objectives.desc: Collect the DC's LDAP log, the flow summary, and IT's change calendar.
hints: Three nodes: DC-01, NETFLOW-01, IT-ADM-03.
Press E at each.
Open the LDAP log, the flow summary, and the change calendar.

objectives.title: Rebuild the discovery sequence
objectives.desc: Press L and order the adversary's steps.

events.label: cmd.exe launched under stolen t.brooks credentials (logon type 9)
whoami /groups: what can this account do?
net group "Domain Admins" / "Backup Operators": who matters?
nltest /dclist: where are the domain controllers?
Port 445 sweep: which systems are reachable?

objectives.success: Who am I, who matters, where's the DC, what exists, what's reachable. Every intruder asks the same questions.
hints: Check the times on the proc rows.
Identity first, then groups, then infrastructure, then reachability.
cmd, whoami, net group, nltest, net view, sweep.

objectives.title: Form a hypothesis
objectives.desc: Press B. Pin the proof and choose.
objectives.prompt: What is happening in the Recon Maze?

options.text: Tom Brooks is doing routine admin work from Mira's desk
options.feedback: Tom was in a budget meeting, and nothing was scheduled on WS-FIN-* today.

options.text: Using stolen t.brooks credentials, the adversary enumerated domain admin groups and swept for reachable servers
A vulnerability scanner ran its weekly scan
options.feedback: Scanners run from known scanner hosts, not from updchk.exe on a finance desk.

options.text: The adversary already moved laterally to the servers
options.feedback: Not yet: these are probes (60 bytes) and lookups. Movement is the next step.

hints: Pin the UEBA alert and IT's calendar.
Was Tom at his desk? Was any work scheduled?
Pin e501 and e504, then choose the stolen-credentials discovery option.

objectives.title: Map it to ATT&CK
objectives.desc: Press M and map both findings.
hints: Both are about learning the environment.
Discovery column: accounts and remote systems.
f1 -> T1087.002 Domain Account; f2 -> T1018 Remote System Discovery.

objectives.title: Respond
objectives.desc: Press R. Prepare the ground for containment without showing your hand.
hints: They're about to move to the servers that answered.
Turn up visibility on those servers and stop workstation-to-workstation SMB.
Discovery alert, workstation SMB firewall, full logging on the five servers.

f1.text: net group / nltest / LDAP queries enumerated Domain Admins and Backup Operators
f1.hint: They listed accounts and groups in the domain.
f1.success: T1087.002 lit: Account Discovery, Domain Account.

f2.text: net view and a port-445 sweep found which servers were reachable
f2.hint: They looked for other computers they could reach.

responses.label: Alert on discovery-command bursts from non-IT hosts
responses.description: 3+ of net/nltest/whoami/net view within 10 minutes outside IT-ADM-*.

responses.label: Block SMB between workstations with the host firewall
responses.description: Workstations may reach file servers, not each other.
responses.feedback: Workstation-to-workstation SMB blocked. Their sweep just got a lot smaller.

responses.label: Turn on full logging on the five servers that answered
responses.description: Command-line, PowerShell, and logon auditing on DC-01, FS-CORE-01, BACKUP-01, JUMP-02, VAULT-DB-01.
responses.tradeoff: More log volume. You'll see their next move.
responses.feedback: Full visibility on the likely targets. Now you'll see the bridges they cross.

responses.label: Plant a honeytoken admin account (adm_backup2)
responses.description: A fake privileged account that should never be used.
responses.feedback: Honeytoken planted. Any use of it is a guaranteed alarm.

responses.label: Block net.exe on all computers
responses.tradeoff: Breaks IT and logon scripts; attackers use PowerShell or LDAP instead.
responses.feedback: Logon scripts failed company-wide and the adversary already has its map. Detect the behavior instead.

responses.label: Isolate WS-FIN-0142 now
responses.tradeoff: They have valid credentials and know where the servers are.
responses.feedback: They noticed and switched to working directly with t.brooks's credentials. Find where they're going before you close doors.

puzzle.title: CTF Cache: Recon Maze
puzzle.clue: Caesar's favorite shift is 13. Try: decode rot13 cache
